newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel president outraged by Indian train bombing.
newsitem.headline: Israel president outraged by Indian train bombing.

text.p: Visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman said on Tuesday he was outraged by the bombing of an Indian train on Monday in which scores of people were killed.

"It was with great sorrow, deep shock and rage that I learned of the senseless killing of 300 innocent passengers on board the train in Assam," Weizman said in a letter to Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma.
Rescuers recovered nearly 60 bodies from a crowded train ripped apart by two bomb blasts in the northeastern state, and authorities said they expected to find more victims.

Israeli delegates accompanying Weizman on his first trip to India said they were expecting Sharma to cancel a banquet he hosted for Weizman more than an hour after the blasts ripped through the Brahmaputra Mail train on Monday.

"In Israel, the prime minister and the president would be rushing to the site of the tragedy. We would have called off any other engagement. I am sure (Weizman) wouldn't have minded," a senior Israeli businessman told Reuters.
"It was eerie that we were having dinner without a murmur on the tragedy," another Israeli delegate said. "It was as though nothing had happened."
The banquet was disrupted though when Weziman took ill, vomiting twice before he was quickly escorted to his suite at the British-built presidential palace.
The Israelis' sensitivity to violence was evident on Monday when several members of Weizman's group were shaken off their chairs during a guard of honour when 21 cannons boomed loudly to greet him.
"In Israel such booms mean serious trouble. It can get very tense," one official said. "We fire harmless rifle shots to greet visitors."
Indian media have speculated that Israel was likely to offer help to New Delhi in combating terrorism.
But Weizman told Reuters on Tuesday he had discussed the issue with Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda only as a general theme on global terrorism.
"It was a review of a general nature. Both of us complained about terrorism," he said.
Israeli officials said Weizman had shrugged off his brief illness and planned to continue a hectic tour of India.
"I am feeling much better. Please do not fuss over me. It's embarrassing," Weizman was quoted by an Israeli official as saying when he woke up on Tuesday morning.
It was not clear what caused the illness but an Israeli correspondent accompanying Weizman said two other members of the delegation were also taken ill.

Weizman's engagements during the remaining three days of his tour were to include a visit to the Taj Mahal with his wife and a meeting with friends at a southern Indian air base where he served as a British air force pilot in 1946.
He was due to visit a historic synagogue in the southern city of Cochin followed by a meeting with the Indian Jewish community in Bombay on January 3, the last leg of the tour that began on Sunday.
